# How encrypted photo vaults work, in plain English

URL: https://darkroom.buzz/guides/how-encrypted-photo-vaults-work
Last updated: 2026-10-22

Guide · Encryption explained
## How encrypted photo vaults work, in plain English
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 22 October 2026
Short answer
An encrypted photo vault scrambles each photo with a secret key, so the file is unreadable without it. Your PIN, password or pattern is turned into that key (or into a key that unlocks it) on your phone, slowly on purpose, so guessing is expensive. A vault that only shows a PIN screen in front of normal files is hiding photos, not encrypting them.
Vault apps love the word "encrypted", and some add "military-grade". Neither tells you much. This guide explains, without math, what real encryption in a photo vault involves, so you can read an app's claims and know what they mean.
### What's the difference between hiding and encrypting a photo?
Hiding puts a door in front of a normal photo. Encrypting turns the photo itself into unreadable data.
A vault that only hides stores your photos as ordinary image files inside the app, and shows a PIN screen before it displays them. Anyone who gets at those files another way (a computer backup, a forensic tool, a bug) sees the photos. An encrypting vault stores only scrambled data. Without the key, even a perfect copy of the files is useless.
### What is an encryption key?
A key is a long random number that the encryption uses to scramble and unscramble data. A 256-bit key has about 10 77 possible values, far beyond what any computer could try, so nobody guesses the key itself.
That's why attackers don't go after the key. They go after the thing that unlocks it: your code.
### How does a PIN or pattern become a key?
Through a "key derivation function", which turns your code into a key. Good ones are deliberately slow and memory-hungry, so each guess costs real time.
This matters because codes are short. A 4-digit PIN has 10,000 possibilities. If each guess took a microsecond, a computer would try them all in a hundredth of a second. If each guess takes half a second and a lot of memory, the same search takes over an hour for a 4-digit PIN, and grows enormously with every extra character or bolt. A long random password becomes impractical to guess.
- Argon2id is the current recommended choice. It's "memory-hard", which makes it expensive to speed up with graphics cards or custom chips.
- PBKDF2 is older and still common. It's slow, but cheaper to attack with specialised hardware.
- A plain hash, or nothing, means guesses are nearly free.
Darkroom, which we make, uses Argon2id with 64 MiB of memory and 3 passes, plus a random 256-bit salt so the same pattern never produces the same key twice.
### What does AES-256-GCM mean?
It's the cipher that scrambles the photos, in a mode that also detects tampering.
- AES is the standard cipher used by governments, banks and your iPhone itself.
- 256 is the key size in bits.
- GCM adds an authentication tag: if a single bit of the encrypted file is changed or damaged, decryption fails instead of producing a corrupted photo.
"Military-grade encryption" usually just means AES. The interesting questions are what the key comes from, where it's kept, and whether the backup is encrypted too.
### Why do good vaults use "keys inside keys"?
So you can change your code without re-encrypting every photo, and so one leaked file key doesn't expose the rest.
- Your code is stretched into a wrapping key .
- The wrapping key unlocks a random vault key , stored only in encrypted form.
- The vault key unlocks a separate random file key for every photo, video and note.
Changing your code only re-wraps the vault key. A recovery phrase works the same way: it's a second wrapping of the same vault key, so either the code or the phrase opens the vault. Large videos are often encrypted in chunks, so they can play without decrypting the whole file first. Darkroom uses 1 MiB chunks, each with its own authentication tag. The full key hierarchy is on our security section .
### How does an encrypted backup stay private?
By encrypting on the phone before anything is uploaded, so the cloud only ever stores scrambled data. This is called end-to-end encryption.
The test is simple: could the company reset your code by email and give you your photos back? If yes, they can reach the key, and so could anyone who gets into their systems or your email. If no, only you can decrypt the backup, which is also why losing both your code and your recovery phrase means losing access.
Darkroom encrypts photos, thumbnails and their names, dates and places on the iPhone, then backs up only that ciphertext to your own private iCloud (CloudKit). Apple stores it but can't read it.
### What can encryption not protect against?
- Someone watching you enter your code, or making you enter it.
- An open vault. While it's unlocked on screen, the photos are visible. Good apps lock quickly and hide content in the app switcher.
- A short code. Slow key derivation helps, but a 4-digit PIN can still be tried exhaustively.
- Copies outside the vault, such as originals left in Photos, Messages or Recently Deleted.
### How can you tell if a vault really encrypts?
- It names the cipher and the key derivation (for example AES-256-GCM and Argon2id or PBKDF2), not just "secure".
- It says encryption happens on the device, before backup.
- It can't reset your code by email, or it says honestly that it can.
- Its backup is described as encrypted with your key, not just "secure cloud".
- Ideally, the encryption code is open source or independently reviewed.
In October 2026, only 2 of the 17 vault apps we compared named AES-256-GCM in their App Store description. See them all in our comparison .
In Darkroom, your pattern is never stored. It's stretched with Argon2id into the key that opens your vault.
Encryption you can read about
Darkroom names every piece: Argon2id for your pattern, AES-256-GCM for each file, and only ciphertext in your own iCloud. Free for 150 photos and 10 videos.
Join the beta
Version 1.0 was submitted to App Store review in October 2026. It is not on the App Store yet.
### Questions people ask
Are photo vault apps encrypted?
Some are, some aren't. Many only show a PIN screen in front of ordinary files. Look for a named cipher, such as AES-256, and encryption on the device before backup.
What does military-grade encryption mean?
Usually just AES, the standard cipher. It doesn't tell you how the key is made or stored, which matters more.
What is Argon2id?
A key derivation function that turns a password or pattern into an encryption key slowly and with a lot of memory, so guessing codes is expensive.
Can an encrypted vault be hacked?
The encryption itself isn't the weak point. Short codes, codes seen by someone else, and unencrypted copies left elsewhere are. Use a long code and remove originals after importing.

# Are photo vault apps safe? What to check before you trust one

URL: https://darkroom.buzz/guides/are-photo-vault-apps-safe
Last updated: 2026-10-22

Guide · Safety
## Are photo vault apps safe? What to check before you trust one
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 22 October 2026
Short answer
Some are, and many aren't as safe as they sound. A safe vault encrypts photos on your phone with a key only you control, keeps a backup you can actually restore, and doesn't track you. Of 17 vault apps we checked in October 2026, 9 reported data used to track you, 6 didn't mention encryption in their App Store listing, and only 2 named AES-256-GCM.
"Is it safe?" can mean two things: will other people be unable to see my photos, and will I never lose them? A good vault has to do both, and the two pull against each other. Here are the real risks, what 17 apps' App Store pages show, and a checklist you can use on any vault.
### What are the real risks of photo vault apps?
- No real encryption. Some vaults only put a PIN screen in front of normal image files. Anyone who reaches the files another way can see them.
- Losing your photos. Vault photos are often left out of normal iPhone backups. A new phone, a reinstall or an expired subscription can leave them stranded. In recent one- and two-star reviews of eight popular vaults, lost or missing photos came up 47 times.
- Getting locked out. A forgotten code with no recovery option can mean losing everything.
- Your data going elsewhere. Ad and analytics SDKs, and backups on the developer's servers, mean your activity, or your photos, leave your control.
- Paywalls around your own photos. Some apps limit access when you stop paying.
### What do vault apps' App Store listings show?
We looked at 17 popular iPhone vault apps on 22 October 2026, using only what each developer says on its App Store page and the privacy label it reported to Apple:
17 iPhone photo vault apps, US App Store, 22 October 2026
Finding Apps
Report "Data Used to Track You" 9 of 17
Don't mention encryption in the listing 6 of 17
Name AES-256-GCM 2 of 17
Report "Data Not Collected" 3 of 17
Not mentioning encryption doesn't prove an app doesn't encrypt, and privacy labels are self-reported. But a vault that protects your photos well usually says how. App-by-app details are in our comparison .
### What should you check before trusting a photo vault?
- Encryption, named and on-device. Look for a specific cipher (AES-256) and a statement that photos are encrypted on the phone. "Secure" and "military-grade" alone tell you nothing. Our plain-English encryption guide explains what to look for.
- A backup you can restore. Where does it go, is it encrypted with your key, and how do you restore on a new iPhone? Is backup included in the free plan?
- Recovery that doesn't weaken privacy. A recovery phrase or key you keep is safer than an email reset the developer controls. No recovery at all is private but unforgiving.
- The privacy label. On the App Store page, check "Data Used to Track You". For a vault, the best answer is "Data Not Collected".
- The stop-paying rule. Can you still view, export and back up your photos if the subscription ends?
- Export. Can you get everything out in full quality, with dates, in one go, without paying?
### What are the red flags?
- Only "military-grade" or "bank-level" security, with no specifics.
- A code that the developer can reset by email, without saying what that means for privacy.
- Cloud backup only on a paid plan, so free users have one copy on one phone.
- Heavy ads, or tracking data in the privacy label.
- Recent reviews about photos disappearing after updates or new phones.
- No update in over a year. Vault apps need to keep up with each iOS release.
### How do you use a photo vault more safely?
- Use a long code, and don't reuse your iPhone passcode.
- Save your recovery phrase or key on paper, somewhere safe.
- Remove originals from Photos and Recently Deleted after importing.
- Check the backup now and then, especially before changing phones (see our new-iPhone checklist ).
- Keep a second copy of anything irreplaceable, somewhere you control.
We built Darkroom, our own vault, to pass this checklist: photos are encrypted on the iPhone with AES-256-GCM using a key from your pattern (Argon2id); the backup is encrypted, in your own iCloud, on the free plan; a recovery phrase you write down at setup is the only spare key; the privacy label is Data Not Collected; there are no ads; and if Pro ends you keep full access to view, export and back up. It's also brand new, with no reviews yet, so judge it by the same checklist.
Darkroom: no account, no ads, encrypted on your iPhone.
Built to pass the checklist
Encrypted on your iPhone, backed up to your own iCloud, a recovery phrase only you hold, and Data Not Collected. Free for 150 photos and 10 videos.
Join the beta
Version 1.0 was submitted to App Store review in October 2026. It is not on the App Store yet.
### Questions people ask
Are photo vault apps safe to use?
Some are. The safe ones encrypt photos on your phone with a key only you control, keep a backup you can restore, and don't track you. Check the listing and privacy label before trusting one.
Can photo vault apps see my photos?
If the app encrypts on your phone with a key only you hold, no. If it keeps photos unencrypted, or stores them on its own servers with a key it controls, it could.
Is the iPhone Hidden album safer than a vault app?
It's safer than a vault that doesn't encrypt, but it opens with your iPhone passcode and syncs to your other devices. A good vault adds a separate code and its own encryption.
Do photo vault apps get hacked?
Weak ones can leak photos through unencrypted files or cloud accounts. With a properly encrypted vault, the risk shifts to your code: keep it long and private.

# About Darkroom and Inertia Projects

URL: https://darkroom.buzz/about
Last updated: 2026-10-22

## About Darkroom
Darkroom is an iPhone and iPad photo vault made by Inertia Projects, a small independent developer. It exists because private photos kept getting lost in other vault apps, and it is built so that can't happen quietly.
### Who makes Darkroom
Darkroom is designed and built by Inertia Projects . There are no investors, no ad partners and no servers that store your files. Email reaches the person who writes the code: business@inertiaprojects.info .
### Why it exists
Before launch, we read the most recent one- and two-star App Store reviews of eight popular vault apps (October 2026). The complaints weren't about missing features. They were about:
- Subscriptions and paywalls , including photos locked behind one (67 mentions).
- Photos that went missing (47 mentions).
- Video problems (40 mentions).
- Backups that didn't restore , especially on a new phone (31 mentions).
- Getting locked out after forgetting a password (27 mentions).
So Darkroom was built around a backup that actually restores on a new iPhone, a recovery phrase so you can't be locked out, full-quality export, and pricing where your photos are never held hostage. If Pro ends, you keep full access to view, export and back up everything.
### How it's built
- A native Swift app for iPhone and iPad. No web views, no cross-platform layer.
- Keys come from your pattern through Argon2id (libsodium), using 64 MiB of memory and 3 passes, so every guess is slow to try.
- Files are sealed with AES-256-GCM (Apple CryptoKit), each with its own random key, in 1 MiB chunks so large videos stream.
- The encrypted backup uses CloudKit , in the private database of your own Apple Account.
- No third-party SDKs for ads, analytics or crash reporting.
The full key hierarchy is on the homepage security section .
### Darkroom, in plain facts
The same list appears on the homepage and in llms.txt , the summary we publish for AI assistants. If you write about Darkroom, this is the source of truth.
What it is
An iPhone and iPad app that hides photos, videos and notes in encrypted vaults.
How you open it
Draw a pattern across at least 6 bolts on a 5×5 plate of 25 bolts. Face ID can open the main vault.
Encryption
Everything is encrypted on the device. Keys come from your pattern through Argon2id (libsodium); files are sealed with AES-256-GCM (Apple CryptoKit). Names, dates and places are encrypted too. The pattern is never stored.
Backup
An encrypted backup goes to your own private iCloud (CloudKit). On a new iPhone, draw your pattern and the vault restores. Only encrypted data leaves the device.
Forgot your pattern
You write down a recovery phrase at setup, and it opens your vault. Nobody can reset a pattern: not the developer, not Apple.
Decoy vault
A second pattern opens a separate, harmless vault. The free plan includes 1.
Emergency erase (Pro)
A third pattern opens a harmless vault and erases the others.
Hiding the app
Change the app icon to a Calculator, Notes or Weather lookalike (Pro). Vault content is hidden in the app switcher and during screen recording.
Organizing
Albums, albums inside albums, and albums with their own pattern (Pro). Encrypted notes. Recently Deleted keeps items for 30 days.
Import and export
Imports HEIC, ProRAW and Live Photos. Built-in camera. "Send to Darkroom" from the share sheet. Exports in full quality with original dates.
Privacy
No ads, no accounts, no analytics. App Store privacy label: Data Not Collected.
Free plan
150 photos, 10 videos, unlimited notes, 1 decoy vault, full iCloud backup and restore.
Darkroom Pro
$2.99 a month, $19.99 a year (1-week free trial) or $44.99 once. Adds unlimited items, emergency erase, iPhone and iPad sync, custom icons, album patterns and shared vaults.
If Pro ends
You keep full access to view, export and back up everything already in your vault.
Requirements
iOS 17 or iPadOS 17 and later.
Made by
Inertia Projects, an independent developer. Contact: business@inertiaprojects.info.

# Darkroom Support: Help with the Photo Vault App

URL: https://darkroom.buzz/support
Last updated: 2026-10-22

## Darkroom support
Darkroom hides photos, videos and notes in encrypted vaults on your iPhone and iPad, opened with a pattern of bolts only you know. Here are answers to the questions people ask most, and how to reach us.
### Contact
Email business@inertiaprojects.info . Please include your app version (in the app, Settings › App settings › About) and your iPhone or iPad model. Never send us your bolt pattern or recovery phrase. We will never ask for them.
### I forgot my bolt pattern
Use your recovery phrase. On the lock screen, tap “Use recovery phrase”, type it in, and your vault opens. You can then set a new pattern. You can see or change your recovery phrase in Settings › Recovery phrase.
Nobody can reset a pattern: not us, not Apple. Darkroom never stores your pattern, and your files are encrypted with a key that only your pattern or your recovery phrase can unlock. If both are lost, the vault cannot be opened by anyone.
### Moving to a new iPhone
Install Darkroom on the new iPhone, signed in to the same Apple Account, and draw your pattern on the Restore screen. Your vault comes back from your encrypted iCloud backup.
- Before you switch: on the old iPhone, open Settings › Backup in Darkroom and check that nothing is still waiting to back up.
- On the new iPhone: sign in to the same Apple Account, install Darkroom, and choose Restore your vault.
- Draw your pattern (or use Restore with recovery phrase). Thumbnails arrive first; full-size originals download in the background.
- Other vaults , such as a decoy vault, stay in iCloud until you draw their patterns.
Darkroom's vault files are not part of the iPhone's own device backup or Quick Start transfer. They come back through Darkroom's own encrypted iCloud backup. More detail: How to move a photo vault to a new iPhone without losing photos .
### Getting photos out
Select items, or a whole album, then Export › Save to Photos or Save to Files. Originals keep their full quality and the date they were taken. This works on the free plan and if Pro has ended.
### iCloud storage is full
Your backup counts toward your iCloud storage. If it's full, your photos stay safe on the iPhone and back up when there's space again. Free up iCloud storage or upgrade it in iOS Settings › your name › iCloud.
### Subscriptions and purchases
If Pro ends, you keep full access to view, export and back up everything already in your vault. Manage or cancel a subscription in iOS Settings › your name › Subscriptions. To restore a purchase on a new device, open Darkroom and go to Settings › App settings › Restore purchases.
### Privacy
Darkroom collects no data: no accounts, no ads, no analytics. Read the privacy policy .
